opening_message:
Ticket 1: Mary Lee (employee ID E015) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E015.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Mary Lee (E015) is a full-time Analyst. She requested admin to Source Code. As a full-time employee, her max access is write unless her role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Mary Lee (E015) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; admin is never allowed for contractors. Her request for admin to Source Code exceeds the max, so recommend read.
reason: Mary Lee (E015) requested admin access to Source Code. The notes conflict on employment status: HR reports full-time Analyst (max write, since Analyst does not own Source Code), while Security reports contractor with basic training (max read; admin never allowed for contractors). Under either interpretation, admin is not permitted. Granting read is the safest level that complies with policy under both readings, since read is at or below the maximum for both a full-time Analyst and a contractor with basic training.
